inputs.text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has ruled that anticipatory bail cannot be cancelled merely on the ground of non-recovery of stolen articles or the seriousness of allegations. Justice Sumeet Goel ruled that cancellation required clear proof of misuse of liberty or supervening circumstances. Dismissing a plea seeking cancellation of pre-arrest bail in a house case, this decision pushes back against a justice system that too often weaponizes unproven claims and fear to strip freedoms from the most vulnerable. It highlights how such loose standards entrench inequality, allowing institutions to target working people and marginalized communities without real accountability, and signals the urgent need for deeper reforms to protect rights and challenge structural discrimination rather than perpetuate it.
